record.paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
record.original_question: For Newton equations u double prime = -partial V/partial u generated by the time-periodic Lagrangian L = one half times velocity squared minus V(u,t), where V is periodic in both u and t, total integrability on the whole phase space occurs exactly when V is independent of u, while potentials of the form V(nu+mt) are integrable near infinity. Are there any other periodic potentials V for which the system is totally integrable at infinity, meaning for sufficiently large absolute momentum?

evidence.quote: Are there any other potentials which are totally integrable at infinity?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider Newton's equation
  ü = -∂V/∂u,
where u ∈ ℝⁿ, generated by the Lagrangian
  L(u, u̇, t) = ½|u̇|² − V(u, t),
with V : ℝⁿ × ℝ → ℝ smooth and periodic in each component of u and in t (with respect to some lattice in ℝⁿ × ℝ). The corresponding Hamiltonian system on T*ℝⁿ × ℝ/ℤ is called totally integrable at infinity if there exists R > 0 such that the region {(u, p, t) : |p| ≥ R} is foliated by invariant Lagrangian tori on which the dynamics is conjugate to a linear flow (equivalently, the time-1 map admits a neighborhood of infinity filled by invariant Lagrangian tori homologous to the zero section).

Known cases:
 • V independent of u gives total integrability on the whole phase space.
 • Potentials of the form V(u, t) = W(ν·u + m t) for fixed (ν, m) ∈ ℤⁿ × ℤ are totally integrable at infinity.

Question: Are there any other periodic potentials V(u, t) for which the system is totally integrable at infinity? Equivalently, classify all periodic potentials V whose associated time-periodic Newton system possesses, for sufficiently large momentum, a foliation by invariant Lagrangian tori homologous to the zero section.
artifact.status_search_result: For spatial dimension n ≥ 3, Bialy (Calc. Var. PDE, 2016) proved that if a neighborhood of infinity is filled by invariant Lagrangian tori homologous to the zero section then V must be (a function of) the linear combination ν·u + mt — i.e., no new examples beyond the known ones. The statement fails for n = 1, and the n = 2 case remains open.

status_evidence.title: On Newton equations which are totally integrable at infinity — Tel Aviv University
status_evidence.snippet: If for the time-1 map of the Hamiltonian flow there exists a neighborhood of infinity filled by invariant Lagrangian tori homologous to the zero section, then the potential must be constant; the statement is false for n=1 and remains unknown for n=2.
status_evidence.claim: Resolved in dimension ≥ 3 by Bialy (2016); open in dimension 2; false in dimension 1.
